chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a debt of one hundred Kurra of dates owed to him by another man, and he has palm trees. So he goes to him and says, 'Give me this palm tree of yours in exchange for what is upon you (the debt).' It was as if he (peace be upon him) disliked it.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And I asked him about two men who share palm trees between them, so one of them says to his companion, 'Either you take this palm tree for such and such a specified measurement, or you give me half of this measurement, whether it increases or decreases, or else I take it for that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, there is no problem with it.'

key_terms.كُرِّ: A unit of volume/measurement for dates
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay off a debt of dates with palm trees using a specific measurement?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the distinction between *Qard* (loan) and *Bay'* (sale) in debt settlement, highlighting the Imam's preference for precise valuation to avoid *Gharar* (uncertainty). It establishes that while swapping a debt for an asset is permissible, the agreement must specify whether the quantity is fixed or variable to ensure fairness, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on clarity in commercial contracts. This ruling underpins the concept of *Sulh* (settlement) in Shia fiqh, allowing parties to resolve obligations through asset transfer provided the terms are unambiguous.
